prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1110; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant, who reports being rear-ended at a traffic light while stopped in their vehicle. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has agreed to provide a recorded statement.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the reported collision. Requested the police report and photos from the scene.

Entry 3: Police report and scene photos received. Responding officer and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and that the collision occurred as described. The other driver has given a consistent account. Rear damage on the claimant's vehicle appears largely consistent with the described impact.

Entry 4: Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness and has been evaluated and treated. The reported injury fits the type and force of this kind of crash. Treatment has followed a typical course and symptoms have eased as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the neck or upper back is known from records or the claimant's statements.

Entry 5: Follow-up recorded statement taken. The claimant added a few minor details, such as the exact position of a vehicle, but the core account has not changed. A neighbor has mentioned seeing the vehicle with body damage some weeks before the claimed date. This has not been verified, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the repair history.

Entry 6: Reviewed the neighbor comment against the collision facts, photos and witness statements, which continue to support the claimed accident. Will ask the neighbor for a short statement and check prior repair and inspection records before closing the file.
